title: The Robin
phrases: a round body on thin legs

doing.t: is puffed up into a round ball
is singing with its head tipped back
is tilting its head to one side
is looking at a crumb of cheese
is shaking out its wet feathers after a bath

close: Just the robin, close enough to see every feather on its orange breast.
Only the robin, round and plump, in the middle of the page.

roles.main: for the orange breast and face
roles.dark: for the eye, the beak and the shadow under the wing
roles.light: for the white belly and the shine in the eye
roles.accent: for the faint blue edge round the breast, pressed lightly

firstMark: Start with the eye: one round dot of {dark}, leaving a pinprick of paper for the shine.
Start with the curve of the breast in one smooth line of {main}.

title: The Wren
phrases: a short tail sticking straight up
a pale stripe over the eye

doing.t: is singing with its tail sticking straight up
is creeping along with its head down
is calling out with its wings half open
is carrying a beakful of moss

close: Just the wren, close enough to show the fine stripes on its wings.
Only the wren, very small, in the middle of a big white page.

roles.main: for the warm brown back and wings
roles.dark: for the fine stripes and the eye
roles.light: for the pale stripe over the eye
roles.accent: for the thin pinkish legs

firstMark: Start with the tail: three short strokes of {main}, pointing up.
Start with the eye: a single dot of {dark}, with the pale stripe above it left as bare paper.

title: The Blue Tit
phrases: white cheeks with a dark eye stripe

doing.t: is pecking a sunflower seed held under one foot
is pulling strips off a paper seed packet
is fluffing up and shaking its feathers
is poking its head out of a nest box
is hanging upside down from a twig

close: Just the blue tit, with its blue cap and yellow front.
Only the blue tit, about life size, with plain paper round it.

roles.main: for the yellow breast
roles.dark: for the eye, the eye stripe and the dark chin
roles.light: for the white cheeks
roles.accent: for the blue cap

firstMark: Start with the dark stripe through the eye in one sharp line of {dark}.
Start with the blue cap: a small curved patch of {accent} on top of the head.

title: The Long-Tailed Tit

doing.t: is fluffed into a ball with its tail sticking out
is clinging on sideways with its tail curved round
is balancing with its tail held out straight
is carrying a strand of cobweb in its beak
is stretching up tall with its tail hanging down

close: Just the long-tailed tit: a round body with a tail longer than the rest of it.
Only the long-tailed tit, with the whole length of its tail on the page.

roles.main: for the rosy pink on the shoulders and sides
roles.dark: for the dark stripe over the eye and the tail
roles.light: for the white crown and breast
roles.accent: for the red ring around the eye

firstMark: Start with the tail: one long, tapering stroke of {dark}, longer than the body.
Start with the dark stripe that runs from the eye back over the head, in {dark}.

title: The Goldfinch
phrases: black wings with a yellow stripe

doing.t: is singing with its head raised
is opening its wings to show the yellow stripe
is perched with its red face turned sideways
is pulling seeds out of a spiky teasel head
is pulling fluffy seeds from a thistle

close: Just the goldfinch, close up, so every colour shows.
Only the goldfinch, side on, with plain paper all round it.

roles.main: for the warm golden back and breast
roles.dark: for the dark wings and the cap
roles.light: for the white cheeks and wing spots
roles.accent: for the red face

firstMark: Start with the red face: a small patch of {accent} round the base of the beak.
Start with the cap: a neat band of {dark} across the top of the head.

title: The Blackbird
phrases: an orange ring round the eye

doing.t: is singing with its orange beak wide open
is hopping along with its tail up
is stretching one wing and one leg out
is flicking dry leaves aside with its beak
is pecking a hole in a bruised apple

close: Just the blackbird, with its orange beak and eye ring.
Only the blackbird, side on, black against plain white paper.

roles.main: for the black body
roles.dark: for the deepest shadows under the wing and tail
roles.light: for the blue shine along the back and wings
roles.accent: for the orange beak and eye ring

firstMark: Start with the beak: a small wedge of {accent}, then the ring round the eye.
Start with the head in {main}, working around a ring of bare paper for the eye.

title: The Song Thrush
phrases: a cream front with dark spots

doing.t: is singing with its beak pointed at the sky
is turning to show its spotty front
is sitting with one foot tucked up
is swallowing a red berry whole

close: Just the song thrush, close enough to draw every spot on its front.
Only the song thrush, side on, on plain paper.

roles.main: for the mid-brown back and wings
roles.dark: for the spots and the eye
roles.light: for the cream breast
roles.accent: for the light tan patches on its sides

firstMark: Start with the spots: small arrow shapes of {dark}, larger towards the bottom.
Start with the eye: a round dot of {dark}, then the brown head above it in {main}.

title: The Kingfisher

doing.t: is sitting very still with its beak pointing down
is turning its head to look sideways
is shaking water drops off its feathers
is flying low and straight with its wings out

close: Just the kingfisher, from the tip of its long beak to its short tail.
Only the kingfisher, side on, so the orange and the blue both show.

roles.main: for the turquoise back and crown
roles.dark: for the long beak and the eye
roles.light: for the white throat and neck patch
roles.accent: for the coral-red feet

firstMark: Start with the long beak: two straight lines of {dark} meeting in a point.
Start with the band of {main} across the top of the head.

title: The Heron
phrases: a tall grey bird on long legs
a black stripe over the eye

doing.t: is standing still on one leg
is hunched up with its neck pulled in
is stepping slowly forward on long legs
is looking down with its neck stretched out
is flying away with its legs trailing behind

close: Just the heron, drawn big, with its long legs and long beak.
Only the heron, from beak to toes, with plain paper all round it.

roles.main: for the back and wings, pressed lightly to a soft grey
roles.dark: for the dark crest and the stripe down the neck
roles.light: for the white neck and face
roles.accent: for the yellow beak and eye

firstMark: Start with the dark stripe behind the eye: one long, thin line of {dark}.
Start with the beak: a long, narrow point of {accent}.

title: The Barn Owl
phrases: a white front and dark eyes

doing.t: is staring straight ahead with its dark eyes
is tilting its face to one side
is cleaning the feathers on its chest
is flying low with its face turned down
is hovering with its pale wings spread wide

close: Just the barn owl, with its white heart-shaped face.
Only the barn owl, pale against plain paper.

roles.main: for the golden back and wings
roles.dark: for the eyes and the fine speckles
roles.light: for the white face and underparts
roles.accent: for the soft grey-brown patches on the wings

firstMark: Start with the two eyes: round dots of {dark}, set wide apart, with a thin ring of paper around each.
Start with the outline of the heart-shaped face in a faint line of {main}.

title: The Tawny Owl

doing.t: is turning its head right round to look behind
is hooting with its throat puffed out
is sitting with one eye shut
is asleep sitting up, with both eyes shut
is standing tall and thin, with its feathers pulled in

close: Just the tawny owl, big enough to show every streak.
Only the tawny owl, on plain paper, in the middle of the page.

roles.main: for the warm chestnut feathers
roles.dark: for the eyes and the dark streaks
roles.light: for the pale eyebrows and the spots on the wings
roles.accent: for the yellowish beak

firstMark: Start with the face: a round shape edged with a ring of {main}.
Start with the streaks on the front: short, downward strokes of {dark}.

title: The Puffin
phrases: black back, white face and front

doing.t: is waddling along on its orange feet
is stretching its wings out wide
is standing and staring straight at you
is carrying a beakful of dry grass
is flying with its orange feet tucked back

close: Just the puffin, close enough to show every stripe on its beak.
Only the puffin, black and white on plain paper.

roles.main: for the black back and collar
roles.dark: for the deepest shadows and the eye
roles.light: for the white face and front
roles.accent: for the orange beak and feet

firstMark: Start with the beak: a big triangle of {accent}, with the stripes to add later.
Start with the dark collar across the chest in {main}.

title: The Baby Swan

doing.t: is flapping its short grey wings
is asleep with its head tucked under a wing

roles.accent: for the shadow where the head tucks under the wing

doing.t: is calling with its beak open
is nibbling a strand of green weed
is following close behind its mother

close: Just the baby swan, close up, so every wisp of down shows.
Only the baby swan, plump and fluffy, with plenty of white paper round it.

roles.main: for the soft down, pressed lightly to a warm grey
roles.dark: for the eye and the shadow under the body
roles.light: for the pale fluff on the breast
roles.accent: for the beak and the webbed feet

firstMark: Start with the round body in a light, scribbly layer of {main}.
Start with the darkest shadow, under the body, in a soft layer of {dark}.

title: The Ducklings
phrases: a dark stripe through each eye

doing.t: are huddled together in a heap
are scrambling over one another
are all looking the same way
are walking in a line, one behind the other
are shaking water off their stubby wings

close: Just the three ducklings, close together, with plain paper round them.
Only the ducklings, close enough to show every wisp of fluff.

roles.main: for the yellow fluff on the faces and bellies
roles.dark: for the stripe through each eye and the beaks
roles.light: for the fluffy edges and the shine in the eyes
roles.accent: for the brown backs and the tops of the heads

firstMark: Start with the eye stripes: one short dash of {dark} through each eye.
Start with three round bodies in faint ovals of {main}.

title: The Swallow

doing.t: is stretching out one long, pointed wing
is cleaning its long tail feathers with its beak
is sitting with its wingtips crossed behind it
is flying low with its tail spread wide
is carrying a small ball of mud in its beak
is feeding a row of chicks with open beaks

close: Just the swallow, with the whole of its long forked tail.
Only the swallow, side on, with its red chin and dark blue back.

roles.main: for the shiny dark blue back and wings
roles.dark: for the eye and the darkest tips of the wings
roles.light: for the creamy belly
roles.accent: for the brick-red chin and forehead

firstMark: Start with the forked tail: two long, thin strokes of {main} in a V.
Start with the red chin: a small patch of {accent}, then a narrow band of {main} below it.

title: The Woodpecker
phrases: a red patch under the tail

doing.t: is pecking at a peanut
is clinging on with its stiff tail pressed flat
is peering round with its head turned
is hammering at a branch with its beak
is hopping up a branch in short jumps

close: Just the woodpecker, side on, so the black, white and red all show.
Only the woodpecker, with plain paper round it.

roles.main: for the black back and wings
roles.dark: for the eye, the beak and the deepest shadows
roles.light: for the white shoulder patches and face
roles.accent: for the red patch under the tail

firstMark: Start with the white shoulder patch: outline it in {dark} and leave the inside as bare paper.
Start with the stripe across the cheek in a firm line of {main}.

title: The Bumblebee
phrases: black and yellow stripes, white tail

doing.t: is cleaning its face with its front legs
is crawling along with pollen on its legs
is resting with its wings folded flat
is landing on a flower
is climbing head first into a foxglove flower
firstMark: Start with the fuzz: short strokes of {dark} flicked outwards from the middle of the body.

close: Just the bumblebee, close enough to see every stripe of fuzz.
Only the bumblebee, drawn as big as your hand.

roles.main: for the yellow bands
roles.dark: for the dark body and the legs
roles.light: for the white tail and the shine on the wings
roles.accent: for the orange pollen on the legs

firstMark: Start with the fuzz: short strokes of {dark} flicked outwards from the middle of the body.
Start with the yellow band behind the head in {main}, using small circles for the fluff.

title: The Ladybird

doing.t: is lifting its spotted shell to open its wings
is sitting still with its legs tucked in
is folding its wings back under its shell
is climbing to the top of a stem
is tucked inside a curled-up dry leaf
close: Just the curled leaf and the ladybird peeping out of it, drawn big.
firstMark: Start with the red shell: a small dome of {main} peeping out of the curl.

close: Just the ladybird, drawn as big as a plum, with all its spots.
Only the ladybird, seen from above, on plain paper.

roles.main: for the shiny red shell
roles.dark: for the spots, the head and the legs
roles.light: for the shine on the shell
roles.accent: for the pale marks on the head

firstMark: Start with the seven spots in solid {dark}, before any red goes down.
Start with the shine: leave a small oval of bare paper on the shell, then fill around it with {main}.

title: The Peacock Butterfly
phrases: a big eyespot on each wing

doing.t: is sitting with its wings spread out flat
is perched with its wings raised in a V
is walking slowly with its wings half open
is sipping from a flower with its long tongue
is feeding on a soft, overripe plum

close: Just the peacock butterfly, drawn as big as your hand.
Only the butterfly, with plenty of plain paper round it.

roles.main: for the rusty red of the wings
roles.dark: for the dark edges and the body
roles.light: for the pale rings round the eyespots
roles.accent: for the blue in the eyespots

firstMark: Start with the body: one short, furry line of {dark}.
Start with the shape of the wings in a light outline of {main}.

title: The Pink Moth

doing.t: is resting with its wings swept back
is lifting its wings, ready to fly
is cleaning an antenna with one front leg
is hovering at a honeysuckle flower
is flying with its long wings spread wide

close: Just the moth, seen from above, with its pink and olive stripes.
Only the moth, drawn as big as your hand, with all its pink stripes showing.

roles.main: for the pink wing edges and stripes
roles.dark: for the shadow under the wings and along the body
roles.light: for the whitish fringes along the wings
roles.accent: for the olive bands across the wings

firstMark: Start with the body: a plump, pointed shape in a light layer of {main}.
Start with the olive band through each wing in {accent}, leaving paper either side for the pink.

title: The Snail

doing.t: is stretching out its eye stalks
is sliding slowly along, leaving a shiny trail
is hiding inside its shell

roles.main: for the brown shell

doing.t: is nibbling a hole in a lettuce leaf
is climbing up a stem with its eye stalks out

close: Just the snail, side on, with its shell drawn as big as you like.
Only the snail, close up, with no background.

roles.main: for the brown shell, and a lighter layer for the body
roles.dark: for the bands that wind round the shell
roles.light: for the shine on the shell and the wet gleam on the body
roles.accent: for the golden streaks on the shell

firstMark: Start with the spiral: one curling line of {dark}, from the centre of the shell outwards.
Start with the lip of the shell in a careful curve of {main}.

title: The Dragonfly
phrases: four clear wings with fine veins

doing.t: is resting with all four wings held out flat
is turning its big round head
is hovering in mid-air
is flying fast with its long body held straight
is opening out its new, crumpled wings

close: Just the dragonfly, seen from above, with all four wings showing.
Only the dragonfly, big enough to show the veins in its wings.

roles.main: for the blue body
roles.dark: for the dark markings and the veins
roles.light: for the clear wings and their shine
roles.accent: for the green eyes

firstMark: Start with the long body: a straight line of {main}, in short sections.
Start with the veins along the front edge of each wing, in a sharp line of {dark}.
